subject: Renewal uplift — cost anchoring & usage wedge proposal
messages:
From: Tim Wu <tim.wu@harbormed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Allison Park <allison.park@harbormed.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal uplift — anchor + usage wedge?

Mina,

Thanks again for the catch-up this week. We are starting internal discussions on the upcoming renewal (June 30) and have an ask from procurement and finance: HarborMed expects a mid-contract usage spike for a pilot rollout across 4 new clinics. We need a path to expand now without waiting for the annual renewal and want to avoid a large one-time uplift that skews our YTD spend forecast.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a structure that (a) anchors the renewal around our current commit, (b) allows for temporary top-up capacity during the pilot at a predictable blended rate, and (c) gives us an option to annualize the top-up mid-contract if the pilot succeeds?

Attached is a short deck with expected pilot cadence and a snapshot of current commit/usage. We are open to a short-term voucher, a blended top-up rate, or a gradual annualization. Also looping in Allison for any contractual constraints she sees. Rafael may chime in on performance SLAs for the pilot.

Can you sketch 2–3 commercial structures that meet the asks with an example cost delta? We need something to review with finance by Friday.

Thanks,
Tim

Attachments: HarborMed_Uplift_Deck.pdf (PDF), HarborMed_commit_snapshot.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Wu <tim.wu@harbormed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Allison Park <allison.park@harbormed.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — anchor + usage wedge?

Tim — thanks for the context and the deck. Appreciate the timeline (Friday review). I've copied Ben for pricing options and Irene for legal/contract mechanics. High-level we can do three pragmatic paths that align to what you described:

- Option 1 — Temporary burst voucher: one-off voucher for pilot capacity at a discounted uplift. No change to base commit; voucher consumed first. Easy to implement, minimal paperwork.
- Option 2 — Blended usage wedge (recommended for forecasting): add a "wedge" band above current commit with a predetermined blended rate (midway between your committed rate and public spot). Wedge runs for N months and can be annualized to a commit at a pre-agreed conversion factor.
- Option 3 — Pro-rata annualize: convert the pilot top-up to an annualized add-on immediately, with pro-rated billing and an annual discount tier. Best if you expect sustained growth.

Ben — can you provide a short illustrative example (numbers) for a 3-month pilot at ~1.8x current throughput with each option and include expected invoice impact and unit pricing?

Tim / Allison — a couple of legal mechanics we should consider: (a) annualizing mid-term usually requires an amendment and signature, (b) vouchers are operationally easiest but may limit later conversion without an addendum, (c) we can include a one-way conversion credit if you prefer to cap downside on conversion. Irene can add specific language.

Mina
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Tim Wu <tim.wu@harbormed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Allison Park <allison.park@harbormed.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — anchor + usage wedge? (pricing sketches)

Hi all — pulled together quick sketches below based on Tim's pilot assumptions (3 months, ~1.8x peak throughput). These are illustrative, not final.

Assumptions (rounded):
- Current annual commit: 1.2M inference units/year (baseline)
- Current committed unit rate: $0.006/unit (committed tier)
- Spot / on-demand reference: $0.010/unit
- Pilot incremental need (3 months): +300k units total

Option 1 — Voucher (short-term):
- Issue a 300k-unit voucher at a 10% uplift to committed rate -> voucher unit cost = $0.0066
- Cost to HarborMed for pilot = 300k * $0.0066 = $1,980
- No contract amendment; voucher exhausted, then billing resumes to baseline.

Option 2 — Blended usage wedge (recommended):
- Create a 300k wedge band for 3 months at blended rate = (committed + spot)/2 = $0.008/unit
- Pilot cost = 300k * $0.008 = $2,400 over 3 months (~$800/month)
- Conversion clause: if annualized, we apply a conversion factor of 0.35x of consumed wedge units to annual committed units (i.e., 105k units annualized) with a 5% conversion credit to HarborMed.

Option 3 — Pro-rata annualize (immediate):
- Convert 300k pilot units into an annual add-on prorated for the remaining contract term (assume 6 months left) -> annualized add-on = 300k * (12/6) = 600k units annualized
- Apply annual discount for add-on tier (e.g., 12% off committed unit rate) -> unit cost = $0.00528 -> annual cost impact = 600k * $0.00528 = $3,168 (spread over remaining term).

Notes:
- Option 1 is lowest paperwork but offers the least predictability for forecasting.
- Option 2 keeps your OPEX predictable and gives a straightforward conversion path without a large one-time revenue recognition hit.
- Option 3 is best when you have high conviction to convert; it locks in a lower blended unit price in exchange for immediate increase in committed units.

Next steps: choose 1–2 preferred paths and I will draft the price appendix and an amendment language template for Irene to review.

-Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Tim, Allison — looping back with Ben's sketches. Tim — does the blended wedge (Option 2) look like the right compromise for finance forecasting? It keeps you from a big one-off uplift while giving you a clear conversion path should the pilot scale. If yes, Ben and I will: 

1) produce a one-page commercial appendix showing the wedge band, rates, and conversion math;
2) provide a short amendment template (Irene) that permits mid-term annualization with the agreed conversion credit;
3) provision the voucher/wedge in our provisioning system so you can start the pilot immediately once we sign.

If you prefer Option 1 to minimize legal steps, we can issue a voucher today and revisit conversion language after pilot close.

Can we lock to "Option 2 — blended usage wedge" in principle and I will send the appendix + amendment draft by EOD tomorrow? If Allison needs different legal mechanics we'll incorporate.

Thanks — Mina
